title: Statistical Methods - Sorting Diagrams
introductionText:
Term 2 · Statistics
Statistical Methods — Sorting Diagrams
The Big Idea: A Venn diagram and a Carroll diagram are sorting boxes. Every object goes
in exactly one place — even the ones that fit both labels, or neither.
Say It Like This
Read aloud
"Here are two hoops. This one is for red things. This one is for things with wheels. A red
car is red and has wheels, so it goes in the middle, where the hoops overlap. A green leaf
is not red and has no wheels, so it goes outside both hoops. A Carroll diagram does the
same job with boxes: this box says less than 10, this box says not less than 10. Every
number fits in one box."
Watch Out For
The slip almost every child makes
Leaving out the "neither" things. He puts the leaf back in the toy box because "it doesn't
go anywhere". It does — outside the hoops, but still inside the big rectangle.
Putting a "both" thing in one hoop. Ask two questions, one at a time: "Is it red? Does it
have wheels?" Two yeses means the middle.
Try It at Home
Game 1 — Belt hoops (10 minutes)
Lay two belts or scarves on the floor as overlapping circles. Label them on paper: red and
has wheels. He sorts ten toys. Then change one label to soft and sort again. Ask: which
toy moved?
Game 2 — The number fold (5 minutes)
Fold a sheet of paper in half and write less than 10 on one side, not less than 10 on the
other. Write the numbers 1 to 20 on scraps and let him sort them. Leave 10 until last and
let him argue where it goes.

Ask him to explain why the red car is in the middle and why the leaf is outside. Then ask where 10 goes in
the Carroll diagram — and why.
More examples to talk about
• The middle of a Venn diagram can be empty — if nothing is both red and has wheels.
• In a Carroll diagram, not red means every other colour: blue, green, yellow...
• The same toys can be sorted many ways. Sorting depends on the question we ask.
• Tricky: 10 is not less than 10. It goes in the "not less than 10" box.
• A block graph like the one below answers "which pet is most popular?" at a glance.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Look at the Venn diagram above. What is in the middle, where the hoops overlap?
Why does the red car go in the middle?
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Because it is red and it has wheels — it fits both labels.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Name one thing that is outside both hoops.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: the green leaf or the blue ball — both are outside both hoops.

The overlap in a Venn diagram is for things that are...
( only red ) ( both ) ( neither )

Where does 10 go?
( less than 10 ) ( not less than 10 )

Things that fit neither label go...
( in the middle ) ( nowhere ) ( outside the hoops )

In the pets block graph, each block stands for...
( two children ) ( one child ) ( ten children )

The tallest column shows the...
( first one ) ( least popular ) ( most popular )
